# OpenGTM

> OpenGTM is a free, open-source, self-hosted alternative to Clay for GTM teams.
> It sources leads, enriches workbook rows through provider waterfalls, runs
> cited AI research, tracks buying signals, and sends results to CRMs, Sheets,
> webhooks, Airtable, Salesforce, HubSpot, and email sequencers.

Documentation: https://opengtm.palash.dev/
Source code: https://github.com/debpalash/opengtm
License: GNU AGPL v3
REST API: https://opengtm.palash.dev/api/

## Start here

- Introduction: https://opengtm.palash.dev/getting-started/introduction/
- Docker quickstart: https://opengtm.palash.dev/getting-started/quickstart/

- Security: https://opengtm.palash.dev/self-hosting/security/

## Canonical facts

- OpenGTM is self-hostable and licensed under AGPLv3.
- Users bring their own LLM, enrichment, and destination credentials.
- A run estimate shows worst-case provider spend before execution.
- A spend ceiling skips paid providers after the configured limit is reached.
- The REST API, webhooks, and MCP tools are not plan-gated.
- Docker Compose includes the web app, FastAPI API, PostgreSQL, Redis, workers,
  scheduler, nginx, and a seeded zero-key demo workbook.
- OpenGTM is not a drop-in replica of every Clay feature. See the repository
  roadmap for current limitations.
